analysis_plan.multiple_comparisons: Holm correction within each preregistered outcome family

rules.criterion: The approved age or eligibility threshold is not met.
Fewer than six of eight assigned presentations have valid responses.
The non-cultural attention check is failed.
At least half of valid presentations are below the frozen 350 ms lower bound.
All non-missing primary ratings are identical across at least six presentations.
At least half of presentations use a viewport below 320 by 480 CSS pixels.
Any expected asset is missing or fails SHA-256 verification.
The participant reports not understanding the questionnaire language.
Required native-script or proficiency variables are absent.

hypotheses.estimand: Average native-script by stimulus-script interaction on the latent ordinal response scale.
hypotheses.statement: Native-script experience may interact with stimulus writing system for each primary outcome.

hypotheses.estimand: Change in preregistered script contrasts after adding recognition, familiarity and visual-clarity covariates.
hypotheses.statement: Recognition, familiarity and visual clarity may partially account for script-associated rating differences.

hypotheses.estimand: Training by stimulus-script interaction with multiplicity control.
hypotheses.statement: Design, typography and calligraphy training may moderate selected rating contrasts.

research_questions: How do native-script experience and stimulus writing system interact for aesthetic, premium, modern and trustworthy ratings?
How much association remains after preregistered familiarity, recognition, visual clarity and training controls?
Do blind visual ratings differ from a separately preregistered labelled condition in a future protocol version?
title: GLYPH cross-cultural visual perception engineering protocol
